goal: I want to follow every new thread my teammates start in the Incidents channel without having to follow each one by hand, so that new threads show up in my threads list and I can open one and read the replies.
consequence: If this breaks, replies in new incident threads never reach Bea's followed-thread list. She misses the update while the teammate assumes she saw it.

action_rules.scope_note: General policy for any journey in the channel notifications and message-threading feature area. It names no control that a particular journey needs.

roles_excluded.why: These need typed or continuous input, which the runner does not produce.

key_actions.why: Escape only dismisses an open menu, popover or dialog. No other key action is in play.

regions_in_play: Left sidebar: team sidebar navigation, its channel and view links, and its category and channel controls with their menus
Channel header, with its menus and submenus
Center pane of any in-app view under /{team.name}/: the channel post list and its per-post controls, list views, and their detail panes. The message composer is excluded

regions_excluded.region: Global header: product switcher, global search, recent mentions, saved items, account and status menu, global settings, help
regions_excluded.why: These are workspace-wide surfaces outside channel-scoped journeys. The account menu holds sign-out. Global settings can switch off account-wide display preferences that the fixture sets as preconditions.

regions_excluded.region: Message composer: text box, formatting toolbar, emoji, attachment, priority, schedule and send controls
regions_excluded.why: Content authoring is not part of the actor's journeys here because typing is out of scope. Without typed text these controls only open formatting popovers, and they roughly double the branching of every channel view.

excluded_name_patterns.match: Case-insensitive, whole word, on the accessible name.

patterns.why: Destructive or irreversible changes to shared objects.
Ends membership, which removes the actor from the fixture.
Help opens documentation (often off-origin). Report opens a moderation flow.
Opens a separate browsing context that the runner does not observe.
Writes to the clipboard or the file system, outside the observed app state.
Changes names, content or channel type that fixture-derived names depend on.

Per-item subscription and read-state toggles change subscription state directly (marking a thread unread also follows it: Cypress following_spec.ts:96). A path that uses them would make a preference-driven outcome self-fulfilling, so no notification or message-threading journey may use them.

action_rules.origin_rule: Exclude any link whose resolved href is outside the app origin, or that has target=_blank. The exact-origin guard aborts off-origin traffic anyway.
action_rules.path_scope_rule: If an action leaves the /{team.name}/ path prefix (another team, team creation, the System Console, another product), the runner records the resulting state and does not expand it.
action_rules.uniqueness: A candidate is actuated only by exact role plus exact accessible name, and only if that pair resolves to exactly one visible, enabled element at click time: within the topmost open dialog when one is open, otherwise on the page. Ambiguous (more than one) or missing candidates are skipped and recorded with the reason. Never fall back to a partial name, an index or a CSS locator.
action_rules.modal_policy: While a modal dialog is open, only controls inside the topmost dialog are candidates, and every actuation inside it counts as an action. The dialog can be left with Escape or with the dialog's own close or cancel control. The same exclusions apply inside dialogs.
action_rules.enumeration: Candidates come only from the live accessibility snapshot of the current state, after the rules above. They are never taken from this charter, a prior trace or a reference path.

predicate.accessible_name_note: In v12.1.0 a thread row is role=link with aria-label 'Thread by {author}' (thread_item.tsx:214-218; en.json threading.threadItem.ariaLabel). The aria-label overrides content, so the root text is NOT in the row's accessible name. It is rendered as text inside the row's preview (thread_item.tsx:280-297), so the predicate checks the row's subtree text. The author is Abe's full name because of Bea's name_format preference. The list container is role=tabpanel, id threads-list, data-testid threads_list (thread_list.tsx:262-267). 'Followed threads' is role=tab inside a role=tablist labelled 'Filter visible threads' (thread_list.tsx:196-216, useTabs :295, roles :333-343). The Header widget defaults to level 0, so it is NOT a heading element (widgets/header/header.tsx:19-35).
predicate.report_live: Source-derived, not live-verified. In every state whose URL path matches, the run must REPORT: the exact live name and attributes of every role=tab node; the live name of every role=link node inside the tabpanel; and how the snapshot renders the row's subtree (whether the root text appears as child text of the link). If the snapshot does not expose child text under a link that has an aria-label, the emitter must stop and report it. It must not weaken the predicate.

events.constraints: Posts go only to incidents. Message text is exactly as given, with no random suffix, no props and no mention. The event fires at most once per replay. The runner waits until C2 is true before taking the next action. Any non-201 response is an event failure, never a product finding.
events.disclosure: Every report and emitted spec must state that this stimulus is posted over REST by Abe's client and not through Abe's UI.

success_criteria.qualifies_when: C1 AND C2 AND C3 AND C4 AND FINAL
success_criteria.ordering: E1 fires only after C1 is first observed true. C3 and C4 count only if observed in a state reached after E1 completed. C1 must still hold at the end of the path (lounge still not 'on'). FINAL is read after the last UI action.
success_criteria.path_conditions: Every action on the path follows action_rules: allowed role, allowed region, no excluded name pattern, exact name, unique at click time. The path must start at start.start_path on a fresh fixture. A replay counts only if it reproduces C1, C2, C3, C4 and FINAL on its own fresh fixture.
success_criteria.selection: Among qualifying paths, the emitter picks the one with the fewest actions, then the lexicographically smallest action sequence (per step: accessible name, then role).

budget_semantics: max_actions counts candidate actions executed as the final step of a replay (one expansion each). max_replays counts every fresh-fixture replay, including confirmation replays of a qualifying path. max_depth counts actions from start_path. max_states counts distinct states (URL path plus normalized snapshot). Running out of budget before success_criteria hold is a reported failure, never a pass.

negative_controls.requested_change: Admin: PUT /api/v4/config/patch with body {"ServiceSettings": {"ThreadAutoFollow": false}} (route api4/config.go:37, handler :279-410), and restore it to true afterwards.
negative_controls.feasibility: INFEASIBLE on v12.1.0. patchConfig validates the merged config (api4/config.go:360 updatedCfg.IsValid() -> model/config.go:4568 ServiceSettings.isValid). That rejects ThreadAutoFollow=false whenever CollapsedThreads is not 'disabled' (model/config.go:5276-5277, HTTP 400, en.json 'ThreadAutoFollow must be true to enable CollapsedThreads'). With CollapsedThreads=always_on, the server keeps ThreadAutoFollow=true.
negative_controls.if_attempted: Expect HTTP 400 and an unchanged config. The unchanged spec would then pass completely, which demonstrates nothing. A run that reaches the spec after a non-200 patch is a setup failure, not a control result.
negative_controls.paired_change_rejected: Also setting CollapsedThreads='disabled' makes the patch valid, but it changes Bea's UI. The client then reports Collapsed Reply Threads as off (preferences.ts:275-284), which hides the threads sidebar link (global_threads_link.tsx:66) and the modal's auto-follow section (channel_notifications_modal.tsx:438). Bea's navigation would fail before C3, which breaks the 'navigation stays identical' requirement.
negative_controls.modal_visibility_with_flag_off: The modal section depends only on isCollapsedThreadsEnabled (channel_notifications_modal/index.ts:21; modal :438). The client does not read ThreadAutoFollow for it. Had the patch been accepted, the checkbox would still show and could still be saved.

design_intent_if_feasible.expected_failing: C3: the UI assertion that the 'Followed threads' tabpanel holds the 'Thread by Abe Lindqvist' row with the root text. It is reached after Bea's whole navigation succeeded. FINAL would fail too, but the spec asserts it after C3.
expected_passing: Bea's navigation up to and including opening the followed-thread view
design_intent_if_feasible.why_single_condition: ThreadAutoFollow gates only the server-side participant block for replies (notification.go:251). It is not read by the modal, the sidebar link or the thread list UI, so it would change only whether Bea becomes a follower.
design_intent_if_feasible.demonstrates: That the C3 assertion detects a missing server auto-follow behavior. It would not show that the product regresses in general.

negative_controls.env_override_check: explorer-proto/infra/docker-compose.yml sets no MM_SERVICESETTINGS_THREADAUTOFOLLOW or MM_SERVICESETTINGS_COLLAPSEDTHREADS.
negative_controls.status: BLOCKED: needs a lead decision. No v12.1.0 setting that the admin API can reach isolates the auto-follow branch while Bea's navigation stays identical.
negative_controls.proposed_replacement_for_lead: Server mutant: the same unchanged spec against a server built from v12.1.0 with only the channel auto-follow loop (notification.go:281-287) removed, using the same config and fixture factory. Expected: C3 fails, while C1, C2 and the navigation pass. Cost and caveat: it needs a server build and image outside this pilot's no-build constraint, and an open-source mutant also changes the edition unless it is built with enterprise. Not runnable until the lead approves.

constraints: No screenshots, video or Playwright traces (explorer-proto/playwright.config.ts).
Loopback origin only, http://127.0.0.1:<port>, through the exact-origin guard. Service workers blocked.
Zero LLM and zero vision. Decisions come only from live accessibility snapshots, action_rules, goal_terms and checkpoint predicates, scored by the engine's generic heuristic.
No feature flags and no per-spec server config. Server config is read only, never patched, except by an approved negative control run outside the spec.
A fresh fixture for every replay. Expected values come only from this charter, never from observed snapshots or the fixture factory's output (ids are bound as variables only).
Never print, log or store passwords, tokens, the license or session cookies. Traces hold no origin, port or ids.
known_risks: Unread suffix: an unseen post renames a sidebar link to '<name> public channel unread' (sidebar_channel_link.tsx:152-154). The view calls must come last in the fixture. After E1 the root post makes incidents unread, so that link's name changes mid-session and the runner must re-enumerate names after the event.

Duplicate or near-duplicate names: the channel shows up as the sidebar link 'incidents public channel', the header button 'incidents channel menu', a channel tag in thread rows and a button in the thread-pane h3 ('Incidents'). Exact plus unique matching applies, and ambiguous candidates are skipped.

The dialog also contains mute and ignore-mentions checkboxes plus desktop and mobile radios. Branches may toggle them. Muting does not change the auto-follow branch, but it changes the channel's sidebar appearance.
Collapsed Reply Threads must actually be on for Bea (server precondition plus preference). Otherwise the auto-follow section and the threads sidebar link do not render.
WebSocket timing: the followed-thread list updates live after the reply, or on navigation through a fetch. The replay must use auto-waiting expects, not snapshot timing.

Search budget: the needed preference sits behind controls whose names share no word with the goal, so discovery there relies on novelty. The heuristic may also over-explore the followed-thread view (strong lexical overlap) before C1 holds.
Goal-wording bias: the goal shares words with the target checkbox label and the threads link. See QA-NOTES.md.
Thread row accessible name is 'Thread by <author>', not the root text. C3 depends on the snapshot exposing the row's child text, which the run must report.
System join/add posts exist in both channels from the membership calls, but they have no replies and no follow control.

First use of the explorer with a fixture factory, REST-triggered events, a heuristic search, REST checkpoints and modal dialogs. The current engine (src/charter.ts:14) accepts only explorer-session-charter/v1, so journey mode is new engine work.
